newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank says finance firms healthy.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank says finance firms healthy.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said in a statement on Tuesday that it had reviewed the credit standings of finance and securities firms, some of whom have been hit by rumours they are in trouble, and found them to be good.
The Bank of Thailand (BOT) also said that it was ready to enter the money market where necessary and ensure any liquidity crunch is removed.

Rumours that several brokerages had been hit by client defaults on margin loans triggered forced selling of financially weak investors' stocks recently, bringing the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index down to near three-year lows.

Under forced selling, investors are required to put up money for their stocks bought on margin if prices drop below 40 percent of the purchase value of the stocks. If investors cannot find funds, they will be ordered by their brokers to sell the shares.
The SET and the BOT have all denied the firms were in trouble, but they did not do much to boost the market which remained below the psychological 1,000-point level late on Tuesday, analysts said.

"After having reviewed the financial condition of individual finance and securities companies, we have found them to be generally in good credit standing," the BOT statement said. "These companies have and will continue to operate normally under a close supervision of the Bank of Thailand.
"The general public should refrain from reacting to unsubstantiated news or rumours which could inadvertently disrupt the operation of otherwise healthy financial institutions," the statement said.

The BOT said it has various mechanisms at its disposal that it is willing to use to ensure proper liquidity in the money market. The rumours about the health of finance firms also led to tighter liquidity in the money market.

"We have at our disposal various mechanisms to provide sufficient liquidity to the financial system, such as the bond repurchase market, the loan window, and a new bills repurchase facility," the BOT said.

It also said the Financial Institutions Development Fund, a unit of the central bank set up to rescue troubled banks and finance companies, was prepared to participate more actively in the interbank market to ensure liquidity is allocated efficiently.
On Monday the central bank injected up to 14 billion baht ($560 million) into the money market to ease tight liquidity.
